fast.$description: 100 ms: feedback – hover, pressed, focus, color and opacity. Pressed starts at once and fades out, so a tap feels immediate.

normal.$description: 250 ms: small changes in place – fades, overlays in (popover, menu, tooltip), content swaps.

slow.$description: 350 ms: larger fades and the fallback where a spring cannot be used.

smooth.$description: Perceptual duration of spring/smooth (SwiftUI .smooth: 0.5 s). Code turns spring + duration into a CSS linear() curve and its settle time.

snappy.$description: Perceptual duration of spring/snappy. Code turns spring + duration into a CSS linear() curve and its settle time.

standard.$description: cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1): a strong ease-out (fast start, long soft landing) – state changes and movement within the view where no spring is used.

enter.$description: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1): elements appearing – fast start, long soft landing.

exit.$description: cubic-bezier(0.32, 0, 0.67, 0): elements leaving – accelerate out; exits are always shorter than entries.

smooth.$description: Spring like SwiftUI .smooth (bounce 0, with duration/smooth): no overshoot. Everything that moves – sheets, drawers, dialogs, toasts, accordion, swipe.

smooth-duration.$description: Settle time of spring/smooth – use it as transition-duration with the curve.

snappy.$description: Spring like SwiftUI .snappy (bounce 0.15, with duration/snappy): a hint of overshoot. Small controls – switch thumb, tab and segment indicator, checkbox and radio marks, slider thumb.

snappy-duration.$description: Settle time of spring/snappy – use it as transition-duration with the curve.
